top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks (Katori, Ye) combine a clean idea, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the lattice light shift so thousands of atoms can be interrogated at once, with a demonstration at the 1e-18 level that has been reproduced and intercompared across several laboratories. It opens a regime beyond single-ion clocks and the comb, and the two names map onto two separable steps (proposal and first strontium lattice clock; accuracy and many-body frontier). The citation should stay tied to the lattice and not to the redefinition of the second. I rank the Kane-Mele-Molenkamp quantum spin Hall prize second as a sound, mature prediction-then-measurement chain, and no award last because two mature, uncontested candidates exist.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as WACQT director I work in superconducting circuits, not atomic clocks or topological insulators, so no direct connection to either proposal
